name: Turned Time
description: Struck glass, bells, strings and reeds whose time can be turned over: a new key sends what was fading back towards its own beginning, where it lands softly, hovers or passes through.

params.name: Body
params.description: What the key sounds on. Each body has its own partials, strike, air and way of darkening. Heard from the next key.

params.name: Tilt
params.description: Leans the overtones down towards a round dark tone or up towards a thin bright one. The loudness stays about the same.

params.name: Frame
params.description: Where the frame round the sound rings along. Low is boxy and full, the middle speaks like a vowel and high is glassy. It stays put while the keys move.

params.name: Strike
params.description: How hard the beginning is: the knock, the first brightness, and the touch heard each time a glass is turned or lands. At zero it speaks with no knock.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a new key takes to speak. A slow one is rounder, and its sand waits for it. It shapes only the first beginning and leaves the returns alone.

params.name: Sand
params.description: How long the sand runs from the beginning to the end of a sound. Returning takes as long again.

params.name: Depth
params.description: How far a sound has faded when its sand has run out. Low only breathes; high falls away into silence and comes all the way back.

params.name: Pour
params.description: Where in the sand the fading happens. Low drops at once and lingers faint like a pluck; high stays full for long and falls at the end.

params.name: Turned by
params.description: What turns time: a new key, the glass once quite empty, or letting a key go, which also brings that key back to its beginning. Every glass turns itself in the end.

params.name: Apart
params.description: At zero a chord starts and turns as one. Higher, its keys start spread along the sand and land one after another, and a new key turns only the keys near it.

params.name: At the neck
params.description: How a sound meets its beginning again: as a soft dark wave, with a strike, by hovering in slow light, or by passing through to its other side in another colour.

params.name: Inertia
params.description: How slowly the sand changes its way. Low turns on the spot; high slows, hesitates and leans into the turn before it runs back.

params.name: Stagger
params.description: Lets high keys run quicker than low ones, and a turn reach the near keys before the far ones. At zero the chord moves as one.

params.name: Split
params.description: Lets a part of the overtones run the other way, growing while the rest fades. Up takes every second one, down takes the high ones. The middle keeps them together.

params.name: Settling
params.description: How sharp and stretched the overtones stand at the beginning before they settle into tune as the sand runs. A return bends back up again.

params.name: Exchange
params.description: How much the overtones hand their strength to each other as the sand runs. The same path is walked backwards on the return.

params.name: Memory
params.description: How well a sound finds its beginning again. At the top every return is whole; lower ones come back softer and darker each time.

params.name: Grains
params.description: How much of the sand itself is heard, as small grains that fall on the body and a soft pouring. It stops when time stands still at a turn.

params.name: Beat
params.description: Sets every overtone in two a little apart, so the sound slowly shimmers. At zero it stands clear and still.

params.name: Ears
params.description: Lets time in one ear run ahead of the other and spreads the two apart, so a turn leans across from side to side. At zero both hear the same.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a key takes to die away once it is let go. When letting go turns time, it is how long the way back to the beginning and the end take.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Overall output level of the instrument.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. Each key is a bank of turning sines whose levels, tuning and noise are functions of a local time that runs at a signed speed with inertia; the phases always advance. Partial places are simplified textbook ones for tuned bells, bars, strings, drum skins and glass, voiced by measurement.
